children.topic: Splenomegaly Features: Palpable when > 2–3x normal size. Kehr’s Sign: Referred left shoulder pain.
Hypersplenism Workup: Systemic pancytopenia. Bone Marrow: Compensatory hypercellularity.
Post-Splenectomy Risks: Reactionary Hemorrhage: Immediate post-op shock due to slipped pedicle ligature.
Splenomegaly Features: Huge: Bilharziasis, malaria, CML. Tender (TIBS): Typhoid, endocarditis, brucellosis.
Hypersplenism Workup: Primary: Idiopathic. Secondary: Portal hypertension, Felty's syndrome.
Post-Splenectomy Risks: Iatrogenic Fistulae: Pancreatic (tail damage) or Gastric (short gastric damage).
Splenomegaly Features: Abdominal CT with contrast (in stable patients).
Hypersplenism Workup: Chromium-51 (51Cr)-tagged RBCs (confirms splenic clearance).
Post-Splenectomy Risks: OPSI (2% mortality risk) from encapsulated pneumococci, meningococci.
Splenomegaly Features: Stable: Conservatively observe. Unstable: Immediate laparotomy.
Hypersplenism Workup: Primary: Splenectomy. Secondary: Treat underlying cause.
Post-Splenectomy Risks: OPSI Prevention: Triple vaccines 2 weeks post-op + amoxicillin in kids.
